eq_profile: ZMF Auteur Classic (ZMF Auteur perforated lambskin earpads)

measurement.source: ZMF factory measurement published by ZMF, Audio Precision, 94 dB/mW sweep, digitized from the printed plot (auteur_hats.jpg, 11/2/2021); companion flat-plate trace in column 3, separate AECM210 flat-plate plot in auteur_fr_raw.txt, THD in auteur_thd_raw.txt
measurement.form: absolute dBSPL as printed, 70 points 20 Hz-19 kHz, log grid; digitization of a printed graph so treble point density is coarse; despike dropped 1 of 70 points (11313.7 Hz)
measurement.cleaning: despike window 7 / threshold 3 dB; 6400-7700 Hz canyon overridden by edge interpolation (null, not fitted). Assistant error, corrected by user: the trace was first argued to be compensated (it tracks the flat-plate trace through 2-3 kHz) and the DF pairing rejected as fictional - the Ori session had already settled that ZMF factory 5128 measurements are raw SPL and the DF pairing is correct. Curve-shape inference does not override settled session doctrine.

yardstick.what: B&K 5128 diffuse-field curve, -1.0 dB/oct tilt pivoted at 1 kHz - the pairing settled in the Ori session (turn 1) for ZMF factory 5128 measurements
yardstick.basis: same-rig-family reference (CORRECTIVE.md rung 1); settled in sessions/ori/ori3-tuning.json and adopted here by user instruction after the assistant wrongly argued the pairing invalid
yardstick.used_as: fit target 1.3-6.3 kHz under the +/-6 dB per-turn clamp with the Ori deviation carried: DF over-serves 2-4 kHz per preference research, so the presence fill lands under target deliberately and by-ear trimming is expected. Sizing reference for the bass shelf; mids 200-1000 Hz held to the ear-tuned chain by constraint; above 8 kHz out of scope this turn
yardstick.pending_upgrade: measurement is a 70-point digitization of ZMF's printed plot, not an exported data file; a real export (like Ori's 958-point file) would upgrade treble confidence and band-centre precision

turns.clarify: How to ease off the midrange suckout (Filter 2: PK 107 Hz, −5.2 dB, Q 0.26)?
turns.answer: Narrow Q to 0.70 and soften to −4.0 dB

changes.rationale: Ease cut and narrow it; Q0.26 gutted 200-800 Hz

changes.rationale: Add bass weight against bass-light report
Pull back treble to address brightness

changes.rationale: More body through the 80-250 Hz heft region
Cut sat atop the shelf, netting only ~+1.5 dB

changes.rationale: Dip masking mud that the heft pass raised

turns.complaint: there's too much bass, it's sounding muddy now too. cut it down a hair.

changes.rationale: Pull the bass shelf back a hair; keep eased cut

turns.complaint: I'm hearing some peakiness in the upper mids e.g. higher vocals/guitar solos that needs to be tamed

changes.rationale: Narrow peak exactly where vocals and solos bite
Assisting peak lowered alongside 2.1k

changes.rationale: Hair off the 2.1 kHz peak

turns.clarify: 2.1 kHz peak: original +6.2, you just heard +5.0 (−1.2) and called it very slightly hot. What lands next?
turns.answer: +4.5 (cut 0.5 more) — confirmed the value already queued from the prior turn

turns.complaint: power chords are sounding a bit restrained...

changes.rationale: Soften anti-mud dip, tighten Q; return chord body

turns.complaint: this one is real subtle. things like crunchy bass guitar and power chords, even down to lower male vocals, are *almost* right. half of the time, they're perfect, the other half of the time, they're just slightly too quiet. how do we fix that?

diagnosis.method: computed net magnitude of the live chain, 40-600 Hz
diagnosis.finding: Broad -1.5 dB trough spanning 120-350 Hz against +1 to +4 dB below 100 Hz; 5.09 dB ripple across 50-400 Hz, minimum -1.53 dB at 168 Hz.
diagnosis.explains_symptom: Inconsistency was register-dependent, not random: E1/E2 roots (41-82 Hz) sat in the boosted region and sounded right, while A2 (110 Hz) upward - most power-chord roots, bass runs, higher male vocal fundamentals - fell into the trough and read slightly quiet.

changes.rationale: Fill 120-350 Hz trough; quiet notes were register-dependent

alternatives_rejected.reason: Under-fills the trough, -0.67 dB residual at 294 Hz
Worst spread of the four; centre too low, leaves 247-330 down
Flattest, but +0.40 dB at 500 Hz risks re-muddying a profile already burned twice by mud/muffle

turns.complaint: not muddied, very clear, but now sounding a bit V-shaped... and I hate V-shaped.

diagnosis.method: computed full-range net magnitude 20 Hz - 20 kHz with band averages
diagnosis.metric: v_db = mean(bass 50-150, treble 4k-10k) - mid 400-1500; positive = scooped mids
diagnosis.finding: Mids averaged +0.82 dB against bass +1.45 and treble +2.33, a 1.07 dB scoop. The arms of the V were the existing 2096 peak (+5.35 at 2 kHz) and 7959 peak (+5.03 at 8 kHz), with no band at all between 400 and 1500 Hz.

changes.rationale: Fill the 400-1500 Hz hole; lands band balance neutral

alternatives_rejected.approach: lower the 2096 and 7959 peaks instead of filling
alternatives_rejected.reason: Those levels were set by ear in earlier turns and validated; clawing them back would undo accepted decisions
Overshoots into mids-forward; listener asked for not-V, not mid-humped
Overshoots and centres too high, leaving 500 Hz short
Largest overshoot; lifts lowmid to +0.85 back toward mud

turns.complaint: that's vastly better, but two notes: big fuzzy bloomy guitars don't fill the space like they should, they're there and balanced but there's no OOMPH/wow/oversized feel to them. can we fix that without muddying things? also, I feel that there are peaks in the upper registers that haven't quite been tamed yet. female vocals and guitar solos aren't HOT or biting anymore per se, but they are a little bit forward.
turns.note: single utterance carrying two distinct complaints, diagnosed and fixed together in one pass; the two fixes interact and were checked against each other rather than applied independently

diagnosis.method: computed net magnitude with band averages; both complaints evaluated on the same sweep so their interaction was visible
diagnosis.finding_oomph: Notch at 125-160 Hz (125 Hz +0.02, 160 Hz -0.08) sitting between the sub-bass (63 Hz +2.51) and the earlier 190 Hz fill. OOMPH band 80-160 averaged only +0.61.
diagnosis.explains_oomph: Guitar fundamentals were present and level - hence 'there and balanced' - but the body beneath them was missing, so the sound never bloomed or read oversized. A notch, not a shortfall of bass.
diagnosis.finding_forward: Net peaks at 2000 Hz (+5.76) and 4000 Hz (+3.90); FWD band 1.8-4 kHz averaged +3.24.
diagnosis.explains_forward: 'Forward but not hot or biting' matches a moderate excess spread across the whole presence band rather than one narrow hot spot - so two peaks trimmed lightly, not one cut deeply.
diagnosis.constraint: listener explicitly required no added mud; mud band 200-400 Hz tracked at +0.22 before
diagnosis.interaction: The oomph fill raises the bass band and the treble trim lowers only 1.8-4 kHz, so the two do not cancel; V metric moves +0.31 net and was surfaced to the listener before applying.

changes.rationale: Fill 125-160 Hz body notch; best oomph-per-mud ratio
Trim 2 kHz presence peak; forward rather than biting
Trim the second peak at 4 kHz alongside the 2 kHz one

alternatives_rejected.reason: More oomph but mud to +0.97, near the range that already drew two complaints
Worse oomph-per-mud ratio than the 120 Hz fill
Centre sits below the notch; lifts sub-bass more than guitar body
Addresses one of the two measured peaks, leaving 4 kHz untouched
Overshoots for 'a little forward' and pulls mid back down to +1.87, re-opening the V just closed

turns.side_effect_flagged: V metric rises to +0.38 because the fill lands inside the bass band; judged acceptable since filling a notch reads as evenness rather than boost, and disclosed to the listener before applying with the remedy named in advance (+0.4 on the 750 Hz band rather than reverting)

turns.complaint: certain elements in the treble are a touch spicy, but it's hard for me to put my finger on whether it's the peak at ~3kish or the one around 9-10k. advise.
turns.clarify: Which region: the 2 kHz peak (there is no 3 kHz peak - 3.2 kHz is a dip at -0.15, so a 2 kHz peak is likely being localized high), or the broad 7-10 kHz lift? Discriminator offered: 7-10 kHz shows on cymbals, hi-hats and sibilant tails as glassy sizzle riding over everything; 2 kHz shows on snare crack, brass and pick attack as forward projection in note attacks.
turns.assistant_initial_hypothesis: 7-10 kHz, reasoning that its breadth (Q0.98, +4.42 dB average across nearly two octaves) reads as tonal character while a narrow 2 kHz peak reads as forward rather than spicy
turns.answer: Neither - the peak BETWEEN 2k and 8k, identified visually on the response graph. Rest of the treble reported as incredibly clear, clean and correct. Reference tracks given: Purity Ring 'Fineshrine' and 'Crawlersout' - high-pitched vocals and dense top-end energy, solidly spicy.

diagnosis.method: swept 3.2-5.2 kHz for the true local maximum, then simulated each candidate cut and tracked where the peak moved
diagnosis.finding: Bump peaks at 3922 Hz (+3.13 dB), average +2.30 across 3.4-4.6 kHz. It is not a boost: it is the unattenuated gap between the existing 3161 Hz (-2.7) and 5575 Hz (-7.5) cuts, with the 3901 band sitting on top of it.
diagnosis.key_insight: Cutting the 3901 band alone relocates the peak instead of flattening it - as the cut deepens the maximum migrates 3922 -> 3963 -> 4125 -> 4364 -> 4452 Hz, exposing the 4.3-4.5 kHz shoulder, which is exactly where high female vocals get edgy. The fix therefore needs a second stage to catch the shoulder.
diagnosis.constraint: listener explicitly reported the rest of the treble as correct, so 2 kHz and 7-10 kHz had to be held

changes.rationale: Remove boost sitting on the gap between two cuts
Catch the 4.3-4.5k shoulder the cut would expose

alternatives_rejected.reason: The assistant's own first hypothesis; ruled out by the listener, who reported 7-10 kHz as correct
Insufficient; bump still clearly present
Leaves the exposed shoulder at 4364 Hz
Lowest band average but relocates the peak to 4452 rather than flattening it
Leaves the 3901 boost in place, so the original peak survives

turns.complaint: yeah, there's some spiciness up higher now
turns.assistant_initial_hypothesis: The 6.3-7.5 kHz climb out of the 5575 Hz dip into the 7959 Hz peak - reasoned as relative exposure, since that region was unchanged but had just had 1.5 dB removed below it. Proposed a dip at 6800 Hz.
turns.listener_refinement: ok, actually, I think that region might be fine. I'm looking at the spectrogram from the HQPlayer Client now, and the high parts that are bothering me are at 7-9k almost exactly
turns.evidence_type: listener spectrogram (HQPlayer Client) overrode assistant curve-shape inference

diagnosis.method: after the spectrogram placed the problem at 7-9 kHz, measured that band directly and compared reducing the 7959 band's gain against notching it
diagnosis.finding: 7-9 kHz averaged +4.69 dB with the maximum at +4.96 dB at 7917 Hz - the 7959 band itself (+5.5, Q0.98), not the skirt below it.
diagnosis.assistant_error: Inferring from curve shape, the assistant attributed the new spiciness to the 6.3-7.5 kHz climb because that slope was steep and had been newly exposed. The reasoning was self-consistent but wrong; only the listener's spectrogram distinguished the two candidate regions.
diagnosis.key_insight: A notch deliberately narrower than the peak it sits on (Q2.2 against Q0.98) carves out the flagged band while leaving that peak's skirts intact - the air above 10 kHz and the 5.5-7 kHz region. Reducing the broad band's gain to reach the same 7-9 kHz level would have cost 0.39 dB more above 10 kHz.
diagnosis.constraint: listener had repeatedly reported the upper treble as clear and correct; only the 7-9 kHz band was to move

changes.rationale: Notch 7-9k; narrower than the peak so its skirts survive

alternatives_rejected.reason: The assistant's pre-spectrogram proposal; dropped once the listener confirmed 6.3-7.5 kHz was fine - it would have shaved the wrong side of the peak
Reaches the same 7-9 kHz level but costs 0.39 dB more above 10 kHz because the band is broad
Overshoots and takes still more air with it
Larger cut held in reserve; undershooting preferred with the target this close

turns.complaint: hmm... I'm not sure about that last one. it's a very fine line between sparkle and spice, but we'll find it. that said, this took away some of the magic and sparkle from the trebe in a way I'm having a hard time putting my finger on. it's not spicy anymore, but it's not quite as insanely clear or correct anymore. we've taken a step away from that. also, Purity Rings' vocals have taken a hit as well with the last round it sounds like
turns.regression_of: the previous turn's 8000 Hz notch at -1.2 dB Q2.2, which fixed the reported spice but degraded two things that were previously correct

diagnosis.method: selectivity probe - measured peak reduction against band-average reduction across notch shapes from Q2.2 to Q8.0, seeking a cut that lowers the peak while preserving broadband energy
diagnosis.finding: The -1.2 Q2.2 notch dropped the 7-9 kHz band average by 1.05 dB and the peak by only 1.19 - very nearly uniform. It turned the whole region down rather than targeting anything within it.
diagnosis.negative_result: Selectivity (dB of peak removed per dB of band average lost) never exceeded about 1.2, and fell BELOW 1.0 as the notch tightened - Q6.0 gave 0.97 and Q8.0 gave 0.85, meaning a tighter notch costs more average than it removes peak. Narrow notches additionally relocated the maximum to 8.5-8.7 kHz, because the thing underneath is not a resonance but the 7959 band at Q0.98, which is genuinely broad. Carving a slot in it leaves the shoulder standing.
diagnosis.conclusion: At 7-9 kHz sparkle and spice are the same energy; no filter shape separates them. The problem is therefore a level decision, not a shape decision, and the previous setting was simply too deep.
diagnosis.affected_content: cymbal sparkle and the sheen on high female vocals both occupy 7-9 kHz, which is why one cut regressed both at once

changes.rationale: Halve the cut; level decision after shape approach disproved

alternatives_rejected.reason: Marginal selectivity gain and relocates the maximum to 8560 Hz
Selectivity below 1.0 - removes more band average than peak
Worst selectivity of all; tighter notches are actively counterproductive on a broad peak

turns.listener_option_left_open: if -0.6 still dulls the treble, preferring a touch of spice over any loss of sparkle is a legitimate endpoint rather than a failure

turns.complaint: let's knock that 2kish peak down just a hair now

diagnosis.method: swept trim options on the 2096 band and checked the surrounding bands for collateral movement
diagnosis.finding: Net peak sat at +5.33 dB at 2090 Hz, 1.8-2.5 kHz averaging +4.39. The 2096 band is well isolated at Q3.16, so a trim moves almost nothing else: 1-1.5 kHz shifts 0.05 dB, 3-4 kHz 0.04 dB, and the 400-1500 Hz mid average holds at +2.01.
diagnosis.sizing: 'a hair' interpreted as -0.5 dB, matching the listener's own prior increments on this band (6.2 -> 4.5 -> 3.8, each accepted)

changes.rationale: Small trim on an isolated band; no collateral movement

alternatives_rejected.reason: Larger than 'a hair' warrants; easy to take as a second step if wanted
Approaching the level that earlier drew a 'vocals recessed' risk

turns.complaint: see how weirdly peaky the region from 50-500 is? ... wondering if simplifying the peaks throughout the midrange and upper/mid bass region and letting the auteur classics do their magic in that region might be one approach to try that might result in a more natural sound
turns.listener_refinement: those tiny swales and humps ARE the peakiness, I'm using the term wrong - I mean how bumpy and rough the midrange response is. auteur classics have really good midrange and bass if we let it. the EQ is doing a ton of work in that region, but it's TASTE tuning, not CORRECTIVE tuning. I want to explore the idea that the current solution is over-tuned in that region.

research.method: pulled every ZMF Auteur Classic measurement in the AutoEq repository - 16 pad/rig combinations across three independent measurers (kr0mka, Kuulokenurkka, Super Review) - normalised each to its own 1 kHz and measured the native 50-500 Hz behaviour
research.finding: 50-500 Hz is the smoothest region of this headphone on every unit and every pad. Deviation from its own smooth trend never exceeds 0.94 dB and is typically 0.2-0.5. There is no resonance, notch or peak there to correct.

unit_spread_db.note: excludes the two Caldera-pad outliers, which run +10 to +12 dB in this region on the Super Review rig

research.implication: the level in that region is not known to better than about 6 dB across units and pads, so sub-dB structure placed there is below the confidence of any measurement it could be based on
research.corroboration: Kuulokenurkka's published review independently describes the Auteur Classic as less mid-bass-emphasised and more neutral than the Atrium

diagnosis.method: decomposed the live chain below 1 kHz into the AutoEq bass pair and the five bands added later, then compared each against the native measurement
diagnosis.finding_artifact: lshelf 105 Hz +5.5 Q0.70 and peak 107 Hz -3.2 Q0.70 are two large opposing filters at the same centre frequency. Alone they produce a 6.41 dB swing: +4.94 dB at 30 Hz falling to a -1.47 dB trough at 156 Hz. That shape is a curve-fitting artifact of AutoEq's optimiser, not a correction - the headphone has nothing there.
diagnosis.finding_patches: the 66, 99, 120, 190 and 300 Hz bands sum to +2.65 at 100, +2.60 at 120, +2.45 at 150 and +2.02 at 190 Hz - very nearly the exact inverse of that trough
diagnosis.explains_symptom: the bumpiness is the residual of five bands cancelling one optimiser artifact. Two earlier by-ear complaints were the listener independently finding it: 'no OOMPH/bloom on fuzzy guitars' landed at the 125-160 Hz trough minimum, and 'power chords and lower male vocals slightly too quiet, register-dependent' landed on its 190-300 Hz shoulder. Both were answered with patch bands rather than by fixing the pair.
diagnosis.key_number: net EQ fine structure in 50-500 Hz is 0.21 dB; the headphone's own is also 0.21 dB. The EQ is adding as much structure as the thing it would be correcting has.

headroom_finding.note: the file still carries AutoEq's original preamp; it was never recomputed after twelve turns of changes. Net chain maximum is +5.32 dB at 20 Hz. Not a clipping risk - it is 1.0 dB of volume given away.

candidates.intent: reproduce the ear-approved contour with the minimum bands; sound unchanged
candidates.bands: lshelf 58 Hz +5.2 Q0.70 | peak 103 Hz +1.7 Q1.06 | peak 789 Hz +1.8 Q1.39
candidates.replaces: all eight bands at or below 750 Hz

candidates.intent: deliberately drop the fine structure and let the broad contour stand
candidates.bands: lshelf 89 Hz +4.7 Q0.70 | peak 621 Hz +1.4 Q0.62
candidates.replaces: all eight bands at or below 750 Hz

alternatives_rejected.approach: delete the 120, 190 and 300 Hz taste bands and leave the AutoEq pair standing
alternatives_rejected.reason: the naive reading of the listener's proposal. It re-opens the AutoEq trough to its full depth, costing up to 2.4 dB at 147-165 Hz - precisely the register that produced the 'power chords slightly too quiet' complaint. The taste bands are not the problem; they are the symptom.

alternatives_rejected.approach: also delete the 66 and 99 Hz bands
alternatives_rejected.reason: slightly worse still, and those two came from the measurement rather than from taste
no better than the three-band fit and costs an extra biquad

turns.policy_note: both candidates exceed the per-turn band budget (amend <= 2, append <= 1) by a wide margin. This is a restructure of one region, not an ordinary turn, and should be staged and applied as a single reviewable diff rather than salami-sliced.
turns.clarify: S2 keeps what you approved by ear to within 0.34 dB and buys only a cleaner curve, while S1 changes what you hear by up to 0.6 dB at some fundamentals and is the actual test of the over-tuning hypothesis - which do you want staged?
turns.answer: S1 chosen and confirmed by ear: 'quite good, I'm hearing more of the midrange magic come back. the simplification is a step in the right direction. much more natural.' Over-tuning hypothesis validated by listening, not only by measurement.
turns.applied: S1 - lshelf 89 Hz +4.7 Q0.70 | peak 621 Hz +1.4 Q0.62 replacing all eight bands at or below 750 Hz; preamp recomputed to -4.7 dB

turns.complaint: S1 is actually quite good... let's simplify further. the bass is solid, but can just sometimes be a little distracting more than natural, and I'm seeing a small dip at 200 Hz that I'd like to ease off a little too.
turns.note: two complaints in one utterance, and they share a cause - handled jointly

diagnosis.method: measured the S1 chain across 60-1200 Hz, located the minimum, then solved for the two-band set that flattens 150 Hz - 1 kHz subject to a bass-average target and a hold on the 400-1500 Hz mid
diagnosis.finding_dip: minimum is +0.56 dB at 204 Hz - the listener read the graph correctly. It is not a notch anyone placed; it is the saddle between the 89 Hz shelf skirt and the 621 Hz peak skirt. Ripple across 150 Hz - 1 kHz was 0.90 dB.
diagnosis.finding_bass: bass 50-150 sat at +2.53 dB against a mid of +1.27 - the widest gap left in the chain, which is what reads as distracting rather than natural
diagnosis.interaction: both complaints are the same geometry. Lowering the shelf narrows the gap from above; broadening the mid band downward fills the saddle from below. Neither fix fights the other - they close the same distance from opposite sides.
diagnosis.key_insight: the saddle is not filled, it is removed. Widening the mid band to Q 0.30 and moving it to 414 Hz turns it from a bump into a tilt, so there are no longer two features with a gap between them.

changes.rationale: ease bass; corner moved down slightly so the reduction lands on 40-110 rather than on the saddle
broaden and lower the mid band so its skirt reaches 200 Hz; removes the saddle instead of patching it

alternatives_rejected.band: single lshelf 65 Hz +6.0 Q0.70, one band total below 1 kHz
alternatives_rejected.reason: the maximally simple option, and it fails. Mid collapses from +1.27 to +0.15 and v_db goes to +0.94 - it reopens the 400-1500 Hz hole that drew the 'V-shaped, and I hate V-shaped' complaint

alternatives_rejected.band: lshelf 68 +2.8 Q0.70 | peak 378 +1.5 Q0.30, bass -1.0 dB
alternatives_rejected.reason: held in reserve. Takes mud to +1.46 and tips v_db mid-forward; undershooting preferred with two complaints answered at once

side_effect.judgment: absolute mud rises, but total energy below 400 Hz falls - the gap between bass and mud narrows from 1.78 to 0.67 dB, which is the evenness the listener asked for. Disclosed before applying because this profile has drawn two mud complaints and +0.97 was previously flagged as near that range.
side_effect.remedy: take the 414 Hz band to +0.9 dB rather than restoring the shelf

turns.guardrail_note: the 414 Hz band sits at Q 0.30, below the 0.5-1.6 voicing guidance but well inside AutoEq's 0.18 hard floor. That width is the point: it is what converts a bump into a tilt.
turns.outcome: REJECTED BY EAR. Listener verdict recorded 2026-07-26: turn 18 was inferior to turn 17's two-band midrange simplification, which 'brought out more of the headphones' natural character'. The 81 Hz shelf and the 414 Hz Q0.30 tilt were rolled back; turn 17's S1 structure stands as the baseline all later turns work within.

turns.complaint: the current peaks create a small valley at around 220Hz-ish. I'm wondering if we could gently fill that in, and what that might sound like. Discuss first, no changes yet.
turns.note: opened as a discuss turn (no changes requested) and closed as an outcome once the listener picked a candidate. First turn of the post-simplification paradigm: turn 17's S1 structure is the baseline and this is one deliberate taste band on top of it, not the start of another patch pile.

chain_before.record_gap: not derivable from base_bands plus the turn list: turn 18 was rejected and rolled back, and the shelf reached 94 Hz / Q0.60 / +4.4 by unlogged by-ear tuning after turn 17. Read from the live daemon rather than reconstructed.

crossfeed.consequence: lambda = 0 means the centre path is exactly flat at every frequency - no centre comb, no centre tilt - so the summed EQ response IS what the centre hears. bs2b spatial vocabulary (level/crossover/compensation strength) does not describe this rig.

diagnosis.method: computed net magnitude of the live 10-band chain at 44.1 kHz with RBJ biquad math, swept 100-900 Hz at 1600 points for the true local minimum, then evaluated at note fundamentals A2-B4
diagnosis.finding: minimum +0.82 dB at 230 Hz, not 220. Left shoulder +2.10 at 100 Hz (94 Hz shelf skirt), right shoulder +1.49 at 624 Hz (621 Hz peak skirt). Depth 1.28 dB vs left, 0.67 dB vs right. Not a notch - the dished saddle between the two S1 bands, with nothing between them.
diagnosis.explains_symptom: spread across A2-G4 was 1.01 dB, smooth and monotone down-then-up: a bass line walking A2 (+1.83) up to A3 (+0.82) loses a decibel on the way, so the higher note reads slightly less substantial than the lower one for no musical reason. Register-dependent level, the consistency category rather than a tonal term.
diagnosis.same_geometry_as: turn 18's saddle, unchanged because turn 18 was rejected and rolled back
diagnosis.audibility_note: stated to the listener before any change: at 0.67-1.28 dB the saddle is BELOW Toole & Olive's threshold on music (+/-1.5 dB at Q approximately 1), below midrange reseat variance (up to 2 dB sigma), and below the confidence of the underlying measurement (turn 17 research: this headphone's native 50-500 Hz fine structure is 0.21 dB with about 6 dB unit spread). There is no corrective case here. The change is taste, and was presented as taste.
diagnosis.why_it_may_still_be_audible: the fill is not heard as a bell - it is a two-thirds-octave slab of lower midrange raised half a decibel relative to its surroundings, and broad low-Q level shifts are the class listeners notice over a whole album (Toole repetition finding).

changes.rationale: Fill the 94/621 saddle; centred on the measured minimum

alternatives_rejected.reason: the listener's own 220 Hz estimate; 230 is the measured minimum and buys 0.02 dB more evenness for free
held in reserve as the next step up if +0.6 proved inaudible
flattest of the set, but takes mud to 1.75 in a profile that has drawn two mud complaints; 0.13 dB of extra evenness does not buy that
drifts high - lifts 400 Hz to +1.93 and raises mud rather than mid. Worst mud-per-evenness of the set
misses the minimum, leaves 300 Hz down at +1.39 and still costs 0.53 dB of mud

alternatives_rejected.approach: remove the saddle instead of filling it, by widening the 621 band into a tilt
alternatives_rejected.reason: that is turn 18, already rejected by ear. Named to the listener so the choice to patch was made with eyes open rather than by default

side_effect.judgment: knowingly past the level that has drawn complaints on this profile - +0.97 was flagged at turn 12 as near that range. Accepted because the payoff is register evenness rather than added weight, and disclosed before applying.
side_effect.remedy: take the band to +0.3 dB rather than reverting - keeps two thirds of the evenness gain for half the density

headroom_finding.note: the structural block still carries turn 17's S1 figure, so 0.37 dB of headroom is unused. Over-attenuated, which is the safe direction; clips=0 on the daemon.
headroom_finding.deliberately_not_recovered: rescaling the preamp would make everything 0.37 dB louder in the same breath as a 0.6 dB tonal change, and level bias is the classic way an A/B goes wrong. Held at -4.70 so the fill could be judged level-clean; recovery deferred to its own change.

turns.answer: 'no, your method is fine. can we back off that by about half? it's good, warmer and fuller, but just like a hair much' - fill confirmed audible and in the right direction, magnitude too large. Reference material: crushing doom metal.

turns.complaint: can we back off that by about half? it's good, warmer and fuller, but just like a hair much

diagnosis.method: amended the turn 19 band in place and recomputed the panel; compared -0.25/-0.30/-0.35 sizings against the pre-fill and +0.6 states
diagnosis.finding: 'about half' is unambiguous on a single band's gain - +0.6 to +0.3. That lands 230 Hz at +1.12 dB, between the pre-fill +0.82 and the too-much +1.42, and takes mud from 1.47 back to 1.20.

diagnosis.shape_vs_level: For a peaking biquad the apex height IS the gain; Q sets width only. Widening the 2090 band does NOT lower its peak - the harmonic-window spread narrows purely by lifting the floor around it. Any proposal framed as 'widen it to bring the peak down' is wrong on the arithmetic before it is wrong by ear.

The macro tilt - warm, relaxed treble - is the Auteur's voicing and stays; 'correct' means removing the measured deviations from the headphone's own trend. This is the Ori-settled endpoint the user had already cited verbatim ('tracing the general shape of the raw measurements, not fitting every sub-db peak'). Every absolute-frame fit was structurally condemned to render as one giant hump.

diagnosis.method: trend-relative structural target: (current chain smoothed 1 oct - the listener's macro voicing) plus (ZMF trace 1-oct trend minus its 1/6-oct actual) via nested eqlab difference targets, canyon 6400-7700 overridden; 545k-candidate search + refine over three replacement bands for the five-band treble segment (t30-search2.json)
diagnosis.finding: under the structural reading the ear-tuned chain was ALREADY 1.86 dB rmse from correct - 27 turns of listening had found the measured features independently: the 1870 +0.9 fill sits on the measured 1.7-1.9k cliff-notch, the 5575 -7.5 cut is the measured 5.3-6.1k peak (true centre 5759). The measurement's corrections to the ear: kr0mka's 3161 -2.7 and 4400 -1.0 cuts have no corresponding ZMF feature and dig into the 4.2-4.6k valley that wants filling; the peak cut belongs ~185 Hz higher and deeper.
diagnosis.in_plain_terms: your ear and ZMF's rig agree about where the treble's defects are. The correction keeps your fills and cuts, deletes two cuts inherited from the other measurement that this one contradicts, and re-aims the big notch at its measured centre.

changes.rationale: structural correction against the trace's own trend: keep the cliff-notch fill (recentred/narrowed per the 1/6-oct data), fill the 4.2-4.6k valley the removed cuts were digging into, recentre and deepen the peak notch to its measured 5759 Hz centre. Chain 11 -> 9 bands.

side_effect.judgment: the deeper 5760 notch's upper skirt takes 0.35 dB off 8-10 kHz; the constraint held it at its 2.3 floor (binding), so this is the bounded maximum, not an accident. The -9 band gain also pinned at its search floor - the fit wanted deeper still and the 8-10k hold is what stopped it.
side_effect.remedy: if 8-10k reads dull, nudge 7959 up ~+0.3; if the notch reads deep, ease 5760 toward -8

turns.staged: t29-stage.mjs lane again: block recognized, recompiled with the 9-band chain both ears, preamp -4.33 folded (the block still carried -4.7; staging normalizes it to the required figure per the turn-20 standing instruction), echo verified. Net audible change vs live: ~+2-3 dB more energy through 3-4.6k (wrong-direction cuts removed plus valley fill), slightly deeper and higher-centred 5.7k notch, everything else within 0.2 dB. Preamp unchanged in effect. Plot t30-structural.svg. Apply is the listener's.
turns.notes: structural features are at the resolution floor of a 70-point digitization - centres and depths above ~5 kHz indicative per the reliability ceiling; the 5760/-9/Q3.4 notch is the least certain element and the first to trim by ear. Canyon still never filled. Turn 29's t29-* artifacts kept as the rejected absolute-frame record.

turns.complaint: so you just extended the current curve without looking at the actual curve. rejected.
turns.note: turn 30 rejected for anchoring the structural correction on the CURRENT CHAIN's smoothed macro - which enshrines the chain's own DNA (including the 7959 +5.5 / 8000 / 10k-shelf trio) and decorates it with measured structure. 'Looking at the actual curve' = the corrected treble IS the trace's own trend: target = (1-oct trend) minus (1/6-oct actual), no current-chain term, everything above 1.3 kHz placed by the measurement. Under that target the 7959 lift is +4 dB of deviation at 8.2k - the actual curve shows 8k on-to-above its own trend, so the trio goes with the segment.

diagnosis.method: pure structural target: difference(hats 1-oct smooth, hats 1/6-oct smooth), canyon 6400-7700 and dropout 8900-9900 overridden, no alignment; two search passes (t31-search{,2}.json, 531k + 85k candidates) over four bands replacing the entire above-1.3k segment, then a hand-simplification when pass 2 converged to two opposite-sign bands 80 Hz apart - fitting the digitization's edge rendering at the data-resolution wall, not a resolvable feature
diagnosis.finding: measured features and their corrections: 1.5 kHz pre-cliff bump (cut -1.0), 1.8-1.9 kHz cliff notch (fill +1.5), 4.2-4.6 kHz valley (fill +5.2), 5.5-5.9 kHz peak (cut -9.5 at the measured 5680 centre). Above 6.3k the actual curve needs nothing the data can resolve: canyon is a null, 8-8.5k sits near trend, dropout region overridden, 10k+ follows raw. Chain rmse vs structural target 2.70 -> 1.10, maxdev 2.37.
diagnosis.in_plain_terms: the treble now follows the headphone's own natural downward shape with its four measured defects corrected, instead of the old EQ's shape with decorations. The biggest audible changes: the 8 kHz region loses the +5.5 lift and its notch, the top octave loses the -4.3 shelf, 4.5k comes up ~4 dB, 5.7k goes down ~4.

changes.rationale: entire treble rebuilt from the actual curve: four measured features corrected against the trace's own trend, all current-curve DNA above 1.3k removed. Chain 11 -> 7 bands.

side_effect.judgment: removing the 1870 band's lower skirt plus the new 1500 cut takes a third of a dB off the mids mean - inherent to rebuilding from the actual curve, not padded back with energy the measurement does not place. Disclosed before applying.
side_effect.remedy: if mids read thin, +0.3 on the 621 band restores the mean without touching the corrected treble
